reviewer.critique: The automated check failure 'NO_KNOWLEDGE_SEARCH' indicates the screener did not verify the employer's scoring policy against the knowledge base, despite it being available. All criteria scores are marked as 3 (exceeds requirement) with no kb_refs cited. Before accepting this assessment, the screener must search the knowledge base to confirm: (1) the scoring scale interpretation (does a score of 3 mean 'exceeds' vs 'meets'?), (2) whether the employer has specific policy requirements for Essential vs Desirable criteria weighting, and (3) any employer-specific guidance on evidence standards for payroll qualifications. The assessment may be correct, but it cannot be validated without this mandatory policy check.
concerns: No knowledge base search performed despite availability - violates Rule 4

Automated check failure not addressed in screener output

4.1.2 For the Payroll Officer role (E1), only experience in which the applicant was responsible for processing payroll counts towards the minimum period. Processing payroll means calculating wages and running pay cycles, not only checking or entering data.

4.1.3 Experience described as "assisting", "supporting the payroll team", "checking timesheets" or "entering payroll data" is relevant but is partial evidence. It scores at most 1 for E1, however long it lasted.

1.2 This policy applies to every stage of recruitment, including screening done with software or artificial intelligence (AI).

2.1 The Recruiter for the vacancy is accountable for the shortlist. The Hiring Manager makes the final appointment decision.

2.2 Screening tools, including the AI pre-screening workflow, provide decision support only. A tool may recommend, but it may not reject an applicant, appoint an applicant or contact an applicant. - a higher qualification in the same field, for example a Diploma or Bachelor degree in accounting, finance or commerce, or a CPA or CA qualification; or
- at least three years of payroll or accounts processing experience, which counts as equivalent to the Certificate IV.

4.2.2 Qualifications are judged on their content and level, not on the name or prestige of the institution.

4.2.3 For desirable criterion D1 (payroll software), the systems named in the advertisement are examples only. Experience with any recognised payroll system meets D1, including Employment Hero (formerly KeyPay), ADP, SAP, Ascender and Micropay. Experience with more than one system, or with administering or implementing a system, may score 3.

4.2.4 For E3 (Microsoft Excel), the applicant must show the named functions, or equivalent ones such as INDEX/MATCH in place of VLOOKUP, or work that clearly requires them, such as building reconciliation spreadsheets."},{"chunk_id":"POL-OVERSEAS","source":"Melbourne Business Services - Recruitment and Selection Policy (fictional)","section":"4.4 Overseas qualifications and experience; names and language background","title":"Overseas qualifications, overseas experience, names and language background","score":6.29,"text":"4.4.1 Overseas qualifications and experience are assessed on whether their content and level are equivalent to the criterion, not on the country where they were gained.

4.4.2 "Australian experience" is not a criterion for the Payroll Officer role. Knowledge of Australian Modern Awards and the National Employment Standards is a separate desirable criterion (D2) and is scored only on stated evidence of that knowledge.

4.4.3 If equivalence of an overseas qualification cannot be judged from the application, the assessor records "information missing: qualification equivalence" and refers to the Recruiter. The applicant is not scored as having no qualification.

4.4.4 An applicant's name, country of birth, accent or language background must not influence any score. Written communication is assessed only if it is a stated criterion."}]}]
